citeAs: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457.
creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
description: A dataset of 7,787 natural, grade-school science multiple-choice questions, partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, designed to encourage AI research in advanced question answering.
name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset consists of 7787 science questions, all non-diagram, multiple choice. They are drawn from a variety of sources, namely questions authored for use on standardized tests.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The ARC question set is partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, where the Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurence algorithm.
rai:dataUseCases: Assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Information Retrieval (IR) Solver and Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) Solver used to partition the dataset into Challenge and Easy sets.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Not an annotated dataset; questions are collected from standardized tests.
null_reasons.rai:dataBiases: No explicit discussion of data biases.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionRawData: No discussion of raw data before preprocessing.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No timeframe given for data collection.
